0.en: The leaf was heavier than anything in the drill.
0.id: Daun itu lebih berat daripada apa pun dalam latihan.

1.en: Jack had expected it to lift like a branch. It didn't. When the padded fork took its weight, the whole blade pressed down on it, cold and soft and much heavier than it looked, and the pole bowed in his hands. Every bead along the edges trembled. The drop at the tip swung a little, the way a lamp swings on a chain.
1.id: Jack mengira daun itu akan terangkat seperti dahan. Ternyata tidak. Saat garpu berbantalan itu menanggung bebannya, seluruh bilah menekan ke bawah, dingin dan lunak dan jauh lebih berat daripada kelihatannya, dan tiang itu melengkung di tangannya. Setiap butir air di sepanjang tepinya bergetar. Tetesan di ujungnya sedikit berayun, seperti lampu yang berayun di rantainya.

2.en: Mark's voice was right at his ear.

4.en: Jack pushed. The blade rose, a hand's width, then another. It bent around the fork like a wet sheet on a line. He could feel it straining to go back down.
4.id: Jack mendorong. Bilah itu naik, selebar telapak tangan, lalu selebar telapak tangan lagi. Bilah itu melengkung mengitari garpu seperti seprai basah di tali jemuran. Ia bisa merasakan bilah itu meronta ingin turun lagi.

7.en: The blade didn't fall. It sprang. It snapped up past where it had been and then back, out over the end of the road toward them, so fast that it whistled.
7.id: Bilah itu tidak jatuh. Bilah itu melenting. Ia menyentak naik melewati posisinya semula lalu kembali, menjulur di atas ujung jalan ke arah mereka, begitu cepat sampai bersiul.

8.en: The drop at its tip didn't fall straight. It flew.
8.id: Tetesan di ujungnya tidak jatuh lurus. Tetesan itu terbang.

9.en: It came off the end of the leaf and straight at them, a round heavy shape as big as a person curled up, and hit the splash board with a boom that Jack felt in his teeth. The board shuddered. The water sheeted down the inside of it, thick and clear, and dropped into the trough. It rolled from one end to the other and back, slapping at the lips, climbing them and sliding back down.
9.id: Tetesan itu lepas dari ujung daun dan meluncur lurus ke arah mereka, bentuk bulat dan berat sebesar orang yang meringkuk, lalu menghantam papan penahan cipratan dengan dentum yang terasa sampai ke gigi Jack. Papan itu bergetar hebat. Air meluncur turun di sisi dalamnya, tebal dan bening, lalu jatuh ke dalam talang. Air itu bergulung dari satu ujung ke ujung lain dan kembali, menampar bibir talang, memanjatnya lalu merosot turun lagi.

11.en: Then the rest came down. All along the blade, the small beads let go at once, a long shower of glass marbles. Most of them hit the asphalt in front of the trough and burst into flat, shivering puddles. A few hit the board. One came over the top of it and landed on Jack's shoulder like a wet sandbag and ran down his arm.
11.id: Lalu sisanya turun. Di sepanjang bilah, butir-butir kecil itu lepas bersamaan, hujan panjang kelereng kaca. Sebagian besar menghantam aspal di depan talang dan pecah menjadi genangan pipih yang bergetar. Beberapa mengenai papan. Satu melewati puncaknya dan mendarat di bahu Jack seperti karung pasir basah, lalu mengalir turun di lengannya.

12.en: He looked down at his left hand.

13.en: The water ran down the pole toward the glove, fast and thin. It reached Paul's rubber collar and stopped. It gathered there, swelled and dripped off the edge of the cup onto the road. Not one drop went past it.
13.id: Air mengalir turun di tiang menuju sarung tangan, cepat dan tipis. Air itu sampai di kerah karet buatan Paul dan berhenti. Air berkumpul di sana, menggembung, lalu menetes dari tepi mangkuk itu ke jalan. Tidak satu tetes pun lolos melewatinya.

14.en: From the cart, very quietly, Jack heard Paul let out a breath.
14.id: Dari arah kereta, sangat pelan, Jack mendengar Paul mengembuskan napas.

16.en: The shaken blade hadn't stopped. It swung back and forth, smaller and smaller, and the stem it grew from swayed with it. And the stem next to it. And the one above that, where the silk retreat hung.
16.id: Bilah yang digoyang itu belum berhenti. Ia berayun maju mundur, makin lama makin kecil, dan batang tempatnya tumbuh ikut bergoyang. Juga batang di sebelahnya. Juga yang di atasnya, tempat persembunyian dari sutra itu menggantung.

18.en: Mark's voice cracked out, low and flat.
18.id: Suara Mark menyentak, rendah dan datar.

20.en: Jack stopped. The pole was still in his hands, held up over the top of the board, the fork dripping above the trough. Mark stopped behind him. At the cart, the rope creaked once as Unit Four took up the slack, and then even the rope was still.
20.id: Jack berhenti. Tiang itu masih di tangannya, terangkat di atas puncak papan, garpunya meneteskan air di atas talang. Mark berhenti di belakangnya. Di kereta, tali berderit sekali saat Unit Empat menarik kendurnya, lalu bahkan tali itu pun diam.

21.en: The retreat swayed. Slowed. Hung still.
21.id: Tempat persembunyian itu bergoyang. Melambat. Menggantung diam.

22.en: Something moved at the opening. The tip of a leg. Dark, jointed, thick as Jack's wrist. It came out of the silk a little way and rested on the stem.
22.id: Sesuatu bergerak di lubangnya. Ujung sebuah kaki. Gelap, beruas-ruas, setebal pergelangan tangan Jack. Kaki itu keluar sedikit dari sutra dan bertumpu di batang.

23.en: Jack didn't move. He didn't blink. The cold came up through his boots, and the water on his shoulder soaked slowly through his jacket, and he stayed exactly where he was.
23.id: Jack tidak bergerak. Ia tidak berkedip. Dingin merambat naik lewat sepatu botnya, dan air di bahunya pelan-pelan meresap menembus jaketnya, dan ia tetap persis di tempatnya.

24.en: Sarah's voice came over his wrist, so faint that he almost didn't hear it.
24.id: Suara Sarah terdengar di pergelangannya, begitu samar sampai ia nyaris tidak mendengarnya.

25.en: Four degrees. It's four degrees, Jack.

26.en: The leg stayed where it was for a long time. Long enough for Jack to count his own heartbeat. Twenty. Thirty.
26.id: Kaki itu tetap di tempatnya untuk waktu yang lama. Cukup lama sampai Jack bisa menghitung detak jantungnya sendiri. Dua puluh. Tiga puluh.

27.en: Then it drew back into the silk, slowly, and was gone.
27.id: Lalu kaki itu ditarik kembali ke dalam sutra, pelan-pelan, dan lenyap.

28.en: Nobody moved for another ten seconds. Then Mark's breath went out against the back of Jack's neck.
28.id: Tak ada yang bergerak selama sepuluh detik lagi. Lalu napas Mark terembus ke tengkuk Jack.

30.en: Jack lowered the pole over the board and laid it on the asphalt. Then he and Mark went around either end of the trough to the lid. Jack looked down into it as he went.
30.id: Jack menurunkan tiang itu melewati papan dan meletakkannya di aspal. Lalu ia dan Mark memutari kedua ujung talang menuju tutupnya. Jack menengok ke dalam talang sambil lewat.

31.en: The water lay in the bottom of the trough, clear and heavy, its surface curved up at the walls. And in it, near the far end, something small and dark was kicking. A gnat, the size of a cat, its wings plastered flat, beating its legs against the inside of the water. It must have come down with the shower.
31.id: Air itu tergenang di dasar talang, bening dan berat, permukaannya melengkung naik di dinding-dindingnya. Dan di dalamnya, dekat ujung yang jauh, sesuatu yang kecil dan gelap sedang menendang-nendang. Seekor agas, seukuran kucing, sayapnya menempel rata, kakinya memukul-mukul bagian dalam air. Agas itu pasti ikut jatuh bersama hujan butir air tadi.

32.en: Its buzzing was a thin, frantic whine. To Jack it sounded very loud.
32.id: Dengungnya berupa rengekan tipis yang panik. Bagi Jack, bunyinya terdengar sangat keras.

33.en: Aiden's voice came on the channel, low and urgent.
33.id: Suara Aiden masuk di kanal, rendah dan mendesak.

34.en: Close it. Close it now. A thing kicking in open water is exactly what it looks for.
34.id: Tutup. Tutup sekarang. Sesuatu yang menendang-nendang di air terbuka itu persis yang dia cari.

35.en: Mark took the first lid section and swung it over. It settled onto the rubber strips along the rim, slow and even. The water rose up to meet it from underneath and touched it, and held there, and the strips held too. Jack did the second section. Mark did the third. The whine of the gnat went on under the metal for a moment, small and muffled, and then it stopped.
35.id: Mark memegang bagian tutup yang pertama dan mengayunkannya menutup. Tutup itu turun di atas strip karet di sepanjang bibir talang, pelan dan rata. Air naik dari bawah menyambutnya dan menyentuhnya, lalu bertahan di sana, dan strip-strip itu juga bertahan. Jack menutup bagian kedua. Mark bagian ketiga. Rengekan agas itu masih terdengar di bawah logam sesaat, kecil dan teredam, lalu berhenti.

36.en: Jack looked up at the retreat. Nothing showed at the opening.
36.id: Jack mendongak ke tempat persembunyian itu. Tak ada apa pun yang tampak di lubangnya.

37.en: Mark kept his eyes on the opening.
37.id: Mata Mark tetap tertuju ke lubang itu.

40.en: Mark looked at the trough, then at the sky, then at the trough again.
40.id: Mark memandang talang, lalu langit, lalu talang lagi.

41.en: Four minutes. We don't carry that. Not full. If somebody slips, it goes over, and we're standing in it. I said nothing gets dragged. I'd rather loud than wet. Four, throw me the spare line. Paul, help him pull. Everybody else, steady it. Walk it back.
41.id: Empat menit. Kita tidak mengangkat itu. Tidak dalam keadaan penuh. Kalau ada yang tergelincir, talangnya terguling, dan kita berdiri di dalam airnya. Aku memang bilang tidak ada yang diseret. Tapi lebih baik berisik daripada basah. Empat, lemparkan tali cadangan. Paul, bantu dia menarik. Yang lain, jaga supaya stabil. Tuntun mundur.

42.en: Unit Four threw the spare line from the cart in one long, low loop, and it landed at Mark's feet. Jack and Mark unclipped from the main rope, ran the spare line through both handles on their own side of the trough and knotted it. At the cart, Unit Four and Paul and Paul's two men took hold of the other end. Jack and Mark set their hands on the lid.
42.id: Unit Empat melemparkan tali cadangan dari kereta dalam satu lengkungan panjang yang rendah, dan tali itu mendarat di kaki Mark. Jack dan Mark melepaskan kaitan dari tali utama, memasukkan tali cadangan lewat kedua pegangan di sisi talang yang menghadap mereka, lalu mengikatnya. Di kereta, Unit Empat dan Paul dan dua anak buah Paul memegang ujung yang lain. Jack dan Mark meletakkan tangan di atas tutup.

44.en: The rope came tight. The trough moved.

45.en: It slid back across the asphalt on its steel feet with a long low grating sound, and inside it the water moved too. Jack felt it through the lid under his palm, a heavy weight rolling toward the back wall, then toward the front, thumping against the metal like something trying to get out. At every corner a little thin water squeezed out between the rubber and the rim and ran down the sides onto the road.
45.id: Talang itu bergeser mundur di atas aspal dengan kaki-kaki bajanya, dengan bunyi gerit panjang yang rendah, dan di dalamnya air juga bergerak. Jack merasakannya lewat tutup di bawah telapak tangannya, beban berat yang bergulung ke dinding belakang, lalu ke depan, berdebum di logam seperti sesuatu yang ingin keluar. Di setiap sudut, sedikit air tipis merembes keluar di antara karet dan bibir talang lalu mengalir turun di sisi-sisinya ke jalan.

47.en: Halfway to the cart, the grass behind them changed color.
47.id: Di tengah jalan menuju kereta, rumput di belakang mereka berubah warna.

48.en: Jack didn't turn around. He didn't have to. He saw it in Mark's face, which had gone gold on one side.
48.id: Jack tidak berbalik. Ia tidak perlu. Ia melihatnya di wajah Mark, yang sudah berwarna keemasan di satu sisi.

49.en: Lena's voice came in, very calm.

50.en: Six forty-two. Sun's on the tops. You're off the edge. Keep coming.
50.id: Enam empat puluh dua. Matahari sudah di pucuk-pucuk rumput. Kalian sudah lepas dari tepian. Terus jalan.

51.en: The trough came the last few meters to the cart. Paul's men dropped the line and caught it by the handles. And then, at last, standing beside the cart with their backs against the cold white side of it, they turned around.
51.id: Talang itu menempuh beberapa meter terakhir sampai ke kereta. Anak buah Paul melepaskan tali dan menangkap talang itu di pegangannya. Lalu, akhirnya, berdiri di samping kereta dengan punggung bersandar ke sisinya yang putih dan dingin, mereka berbalik.

52.en: The sun had reached halfway down the wall of stems. Every drop it touched lit up at once, gold and blazing. Above the place where they had stood, the silk retreat glowed like a paper lantern.
52.id: Sinar matahari sudah turun sampai separuh dinding batang rumput. Setiap tetesan yang disentuhnya langsung menyala, keemasan dan berkobar. Di atas tempat mereka tadi berdiri, tempat persembunyian dari sutra itu berpendar seperti lampion kertas.

53.en: The spider came out of it legs first, the way it had on the cold mornings. It climbed down the stem in short, careful steps, and stopped in the light, and was still.
53.id: Laba-laba itu keluar dari sana dengan kaki lebih dulu, seperti pada pagi-pagi yang dingin. Ia menuruni batang dengan langkah-langkah pendek yang hati-hati, lalu berhenti di bawah cahaya, dan diam.

54.en: It sat there in the sun. It didn't look at them. It didn't look at anything. It sat with its legs drawn in, warming up.
54.id: Ia diam di sana di bawah matahari. Ia tidak memandang mereka. Ia tidak memandang apa pun. Ia diam dengan kaki-kaki terlipat, menghangatkan diri.

55.en: Paul was standing beside Jack, his hands back in his pockets. He watched it for a long time.
55.id: Paul berdiri di samping Jack, kedua tangannya kembali di saku. Ia memperhatikannya lama sekali.

57.en: Jack didn't take his eyes off it.
57.id: Jack tidak mengalihkan matanya dari makhluk itu.

60.en: It's smaller than I thought. No. It isn't. I was hoping.
60.id: Lebih kecil dari yang saya kira. Tidak. Ternyata tidak. Saya cuma berharap.

61.en: On the way back to the station, nobody spoke for a long time. Then Jack remembered, and stripped the bag and the glove off his left hand on the back seat, and held it up to the window. Dry. The tape was dry. The stitches were pink and quiet under it.
61.id: Dalam perjalanan kembali ke stasiun, lama tak ada yang bicara. Lalu Jack teringat, dan melepas kantong dan sarung tangan dari tangan kirinya di kursi belakang, lalu mengangkatnya ke jendela. Kering. Plesternya kering. Jahitan di bawahnya merah muda dan tenang.

66.en: Good. I was about to call Doctor Mercer on you.
66.id: Bagus. Aku sudah hampir melaporkanmu ke Dokter Mercer.

67.en: At the utility station, Paul backed the flatbed up to the loading platform. He had built a drain spigot into one end of the trough, a short brass spout with a handle. He knelt by it with a row of empty twenty-liter jugs waiting, and Lena with her clipboard, and Mark in the doorway where he always stood.
67.id: Di stasiun utilitas, Paul memundurkan truk pengangkut sampai ke peron bongkar muat. Ia sudah memasang keran pembuangan di salah satu ujung talang, cerat kuningan pendek dengan tuas. Ia berlutut di sampingnya dengan sederet jeriken dua puluh liter yang kosong menunggu, dan Lena dengan papan klipnya, dan Mark di ambang pintu, tempat ia selalu berdiri.

69.en: The water came out clear and cold and steady. It filled the first jug, and Lena marked it. Then the second. Then the third, and the fourth, and the fifth. Halfway up the sixth, it slowed to a trickle, and to a drip, and stopped.
69.id: Air keluar bening dan dingin dan stabil. Air itu mengisi jeriken pertama, dan Lena mencatatnya. Lalu yang kedua. Lalu yang ketiga, dan keempat, dan kelima. Di separuh jeriken keenam, alirannya melambat menjadi rembesan, lalu tetesan, lalu berhenti.

70.en: Lena counted the jugs twice. Then she wrote the number down.
70.id: Lena menghitung jeriken-jeriken itu dua kali. Lalu ia menuliskan angkanya.

72.en: Jack looked at the row of jugs. A hundred and ten. Nine times what they had nearly drowned Aiden for. From one shake of one leaf. And it had been the smaller drop.
72.id: Jack memandang deretan jeriken itu. Seratus sepuluh. Sembilan kali lipat dari jumlah yang hampir membuat Aiden tenggelam. Dari satu goyangan satu daun. Dan itu tetesan yang lebih kecil.

73.en: Paul sat back on his heels. He didn't say anything. He took the rubber strip at the corner of the lid between his finger and thumb, and pressed it down, the whole length of it.
73.id: Paul duduk bertumpu di tumitnya. Ia tidak berkata apa-apa. Ia menjepit strip karet di sudut tutup di antara jari dan ibu jarinya, lalu menekannya, dari ujung ke ujung.

74.en: Then Aiden's voice came through Lena's console. He didn't sound pleased. He sounded careful, the way he had sounded on the first morning, looking at the greenhouse glass.
74.id: Lalu suara Aiden terdengar lewat konsol Lena. Ia tidak terdengar senang. Ia terdengar hati-hati, seperti suaranya pada pagi pertama itu, sambil memandang kaca rumah kaca.

75.en: Doctor Bennett. I've been going back over the feed, up to where you closed the lid. The leg didn't come out when the stem moved. The stem had been moving for a good five seconds by then. It came out two seconds after that gnat hit the water and started kicking. It wasn't watching us. It wasn't watching the shake. It saw breakfast. And it was too cold to come and get it.
75.id: Dokter Bennett. Aku sudah memeriksa ulang tayangannya, sampai saat kalian menutup tutupnya. Kakinya tidak keluar waktu batangnya bergerak. Saat itu batangnya sudah bergerak lima detik penuh. Kaki itu keluar dua detik setelah agas itu jatuh ke air dan mulai menendang-nendang. Dia tidak sedang mengawasi kita. Dia tidak sedang mengawasi goyangannya. Dia melihat sarapan. Dan dia terlalu kedinginan untuk datang mengambilnya.

76.en: Aiden was quiet for a moment.

77.en: Every leaf we shake is going to shake one down.
77.id: Setiap daun yang kita goyang bakal ikut menjatuhkan satu.
